tara: Quick thread — noticed the ingress shim maps API keys to project via X-Project header. What happens when customers omit X-Project or send conflicting claims?

devon: Are we talking hosted API ingress shim or the private/dedicated shim?

tara: Hosted ingress shim (v0.3). Example request we see: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: ApiKey abc.def.ghi
X-Project: proj:acme:123
```
If X-Project is missing we currently fallback to the org claim on the key metadata. That fallback seems risky for some flows.

mike: Fallback is convenient but edge: operator/service tokens that can inject X-Project could escalate privileges. We need binding rules so a caller can't impersonate a project just by setting the header.

elaine: Agreed. Proposal: only accept client-supplied X-Project when the API key explicitly carries a project-scoped claim (e.g., claims: ["proj:acme:123"]) or when the request originates from an authenticated internal svc principal. Otherwise strip X-Project server-side.

jordan: How do we order RBAC checks? Do we resolve actor -> project -> roles in one pass? Also, caching: a KV cache keyed only on route+api_key could leak responses across projects.

devon: For caching: suffix the cache key with project_id (or empty) and auth_mode. So cache_key = hash(api_key_id + "/" + project_id + "/" + route + "/" + auth_mode). Slight perf hit but avoids cross-project cache bleed. Keep TTL short for inferred-project entries.

auth-bot: scan-result: 12,374 requests in last 24h from keys without X-Project header — they'd hit org fallback today.

mike: Another real case: internal microservices sometimes forward third-party customer keys in outbound calls. If forwarder adds X-Project to satisfy downstream routing, that could create implicit elevation. We should require a provenance header when allowing forwarded project hints, e.g., X-Origin-Intent: signed by forwarder.

tara: Suggested concrete rules to implement: 
  * disallow honoring client-supplied X-Project unless the API key metadata includes explicit project claim
  * when project is inferred (org fallback), tag the request with shim.project_inferred=true for telemetry and alerting
  * cache keys must include project_id and auth_mode (api_key vs svc_token)
  * require forwarders to sign X-Origin-Intent; otherwise strip project header on ingress
  * add unit+integration tests covering inbound-forwarded and S2S forwarding flows

elaine: SGTM. I'll draft a short mini-RFC with explicit examples and a config toggle `ingress.strict_project_header` so private deployments can opt into stricter behavior.

jordan: I'll own the cache change and perf test. Plan: run 72h replay with new keying to validate hit-rate regression.

mike: I'll produce a list of known forwarders and high-risk services (S3-proxy, ingest-gateway, partner-proxy) and flag anything that rewrites Authorization or X-Project.

tara: Nice. One more nit: telemetry - please include shim.project_source = ["explicit", "inferred", "forwarded", "internal"] so we can alert when forwarded/inferred dominates.

elaine: adding that to the RFC. Also recommend a small rollout: v0.3.1 with header-strip fallback only, then v0.4 enforce binding by claim.

mike: :+1: on staged rollout. We should coordinate with support for triage playbook.

tara: Thanks all — actionable next steps and owners. I'll follow up with a short doc and link to test cases. :raised_hands:
